picked.t: 베트남, 내년 경제성장률 최소 10% 목표…국회 결의안 승인
picked.body: 기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 베트남이 내년 국내총생산(GDP) 최소 10%를 목표로 경제 성장 가속화에 나선다. 베트남 국회는 지난 7일 회의에서 이러한 내용을 골자로 한 ‘2027년 사회경제발전계획’ 결의안을 재석 의원 93.4%의 찬성으로 가결 처리했다. 결의안에는 내년 거시경제 주요 목표로 △경제성장률 최소 10% △1인당 GDP 약 6,100달러 △물가상승률 약 4.5% 통제 등이 담겼다. 국회는 정부가 성장을 최우선 과제로 삼되, 거시경제 안정과 물가 관리, 경제 전반의 주요 균형을 유지하는 데 중점적으로 나서야 한다고 강조했다. 특히 국회는 대출금리 인하와 생산·사업 및 우선 지원 분야에 대한 자금 지원을 결의안에 명시하는 등 국내외 정세에 따른 금리·환율 관리를 정부에 강조했다. 결의안에 따라 정부는 △세수 증대와 지출 절감(특히 경상지출) △각종 채권 발행 △공적개발원조(ODA) 차입 △국가안보에 영향이 없는 업종에서 외국인 지분 한도를 넓히는 정책의 조기 시행 등 모든 재원을 동원해 경제 성장을 위해 효율적으로 활용할 예정이다. 이와 함께 정부는 무역적자 해소 방안을 마련하고, 건전하고 지속 가능한 부동산 시장을 개발하며, 장기간 적체된 사업을 해소하는데 주력해야 한다. 에너지안보에서는 어떤 상황에서도 전기와 석유를 충분히 공급하는 데 주력하도록 했다. 인프라 분야에서는 △계획에 따른 고속도로망 완공, 특히 북남고속도로 동·서부 구간 △라오까이-하노이-하이퐁 철도 △북남고속철도 △국제철도 및 도시철도 등 주요 사업의 가속화가 정부의 과제로 주어졌다. 특히 결의안에서는 롱탄(Long Thanh)국제공항 및 자빈(Gia Binh)국제공항 건설 가속화가 명시됐다. 에너지 인프라의 경우, 국가 에너지 비축 전략을 세우고, 계획된 전원·송전망·태양광 사업을 가속화해야 한다는 과제가 주어졌다. 국회는 각 지방정부로 하여금 △공항 △항만 △데이터센터 △자유무역지대 등에 대한 무분별한 투자로 낭비를 초래하는 상황을 단호히 해결할 것을 요구했다.

picked.t: 베트남 부총리 “친환경 모빌리티 전환, 강제해선 안 돼”…자발적 전환 장려 촉구
picked.body: 호치민시의 한 거리에서 퇴근길 오토바이들이 신호 대기 중인 모습.  베트남 대도시를 중심으로 친환경 모빌리티 전환이 가속화되고 있는 가운데 정부는 시민들로 하여금 전기차 전환을 강제해서는 안 된다는 방침을 밝혔다. 베트남 정부사무국은 팜 지아 뚝(Pham Gia Tuc) 상임부총리의 이러한 지시사항을 담은 지침을 지난 5일 공포했다. 뚝 부총리는 이번 지침을 통해 사회경제적 여건과 교통 인프라 실정에 맞춰 국민과 기업이 스스로 친환경 교통수단으로 옮기도록 장려하는 해법 마련을 건설부에 지시했다. 뚝 부총리는 관련 정책에 차량 소유자와 국민, 기업이 순수 전기차나 친환경 교통수단으로 바꿔야 한다는 의무 규정이나 의무 로드맵이 포함되어서는 안 된다는 점을 강조했다. 베트남 수도 하노이와 남부 최대 도시인 호치민시는 그동안 친환경 모빌리티 전환 로드맵 아래 저배출구역(LEZ) 시범 운영 등 오염물질 배출이 많은 내연기관 차량에 대한 규제를 지속적으로 확대하는 움직임을 보여왔다. 실제로 하노이는 지난 7월부터 호안끼엠동(phuong Hoan Kiem) 내 2곳에서 LEZ를 시범 운영하고 있다. 해당 지역에서는 내연기관 이륜차 통행이 제한되지는 않으나, 영업용 이륜차를 중심으로 운행 제한이 권고되고 있다. 자가용의 경우, 시당국은 2008년 이전 생산·수입된 이륜차와 2016년 이전 출고된 이륜차의 사용 제한을 권장하고 있으며, 지역민들로 하여금 친환경 차량 전환이나 대중교통 사용을 장려하고 있다. 호치민시 역시 친환경 모빌리티 전환 로드맵을 통해 LEZ 지정안을 검토하고 있다. 현재 마련된 초안에 따르면, 오는 2028년 1월부터 2029년까지는 도심지와 투티엠(Thu Thiem) 신도시 지역이 LEZ로 지정될 예정이며, 2030년부터는 제2순환도로 내부로 LEZ 범위가 확대될 예정이다. 또한 호치민시는 2027년부터 관내 모든 시내버스를 친환경 버스로 전환할 계획이다. 정부기관 또는 공공기관 역시 자동차와 이륜차 등 관용차를 새로 구입하거나 교체 시기가 도래한 경우, 이 요건을 충족해야 한다. 나아가 호치민시는 2030년부터 택시 및 영업용 이륜차의 친환경 전환을 의무화하고, 2045년까지 관내 모든 차량을 친환경 차량으로 전환한다는 목표다.

picked.t: Vietnamese abroad stay calm amid governments’ calls to stock emergency supplies
picked.body: Relatives in Vietnam repeatedly called Hoang Van Quy, 32, in Hannover, Germany, to urge him to buy a week’s worth of emergency supplies. Reports that several countries had advised residents to stock up had left them worried. But he saw no reason to panic or anyone rushing to buy food. "After more than four years in Germany, I’m familiar with the way locals plan for risks. They insure everything and always keep a corner of their home stocked with emergency supplies," he said. Germany holds Warntag (National Warning Day), when sirens and emergency alerts are tested, he said. Households have for long been advised to keep enough food and drinking water for 10 days in case of natural disasters, widespread power outages, or supply disruptions in a handbook distributed by the Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (BBK). "The purpose of the advice is to help people manage on their own during the first 72 hours, easing the burden on rescuers. Calm preparation is what matters most," Quy said. In Berlin, Kieu Hoa, 35, treats government advice on emergency supplies much like a forecast of bad weather. After 12 years in Germany, she is used to keeping a stocked medicine cabinet, a rechargeable flashlight, and several containers of drinking water at home. Her neighborhood supermarkets remain well stocked and prices are stable. "Germany’s advice is not simply to ‘buy things when there is bad news.’ It is about being prepared regularly, keeping supplies somewhere cool and dry, and checking expiration dates periodically," she said. In the U.S., households are advised to keep enough food, drinking water, medicines, and other essentials for several days and draw up a household emergency plan. This guidance has been available through Ready.gov since 2003 from the Federal Emergency Management Agency. Kim Tuyen, 31, in Chicago, learned about the guidance only after seeing it on TikTok and Instagram Reels in early November. She went grocery shopping as usual over the weekend, buying an extra packet of noodles only because she had run out. "Where I live, snowstorms often last one or two days, and so keeping food in the refrigerator is a normal habit. No one is panicking." In Toyama, Japan, Huynh Qui, 38, is familiar with government recommendations to keep three to seven days’ worth of food in preparation for earthquakes and volcanic eruptions. Disaster preparedness has become second nature to Japanese following the 1995 Kobe earthquake and the 2011 earthquake and tsunami. Qui always keeps a case of mineral water and emergency toilet bags at home. "Natural disasters happen in cycles in Japan. No one rushes out to stockpile because convenience stores always have supplies available," he said. In South Korea, authorities have issued no new advisory, but many Vietnamese living there continue to keep emergency supplies. Nguyen Ngoan, 32, in Incheon, said she always has several small gas canisters, dried noodles, and bottled water in her kitchen. "People here have long kept dry food at home. They don’t wait until something happens before rushing to the supermarket." Other countries have also promoted emergency preparedness in recent years. In March 2025, the EU unveiled its Preparedness Union Strategy to help people cope with climate change, cyber incidents, and supply disruptions. Sweden recommends keeping enough essentials to manage independently for at least seven days. Its booklet "If Crisis or War Comes," updated in 2024, explains how to respond to armed conflict, power outages, extreme weather, and cyberattacks. Finland advises residents to keep enough essentials for 72 hours. Rescuers cannot reach every household immediately in an emergency, making families’ ability to manage on their own for the first three days a crucial part of civil defense, authorities in these countries explain. Residents should prepare emergency bags containing enough supplies for 72 hours, Thailand’s Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation advised on Nov. 2. The advice by various countries has prompted a lot of discussion among ethnic Vietnamese, for whom the concept is new, Hoang Lien, 25, who has lived in Bangkok for eight years, said. Some people she knows bought extra medicines, drinking water, and canned foods with long shelf lives. She herself stocked up, prompted by the recent flooding that disrupted life. "I packed a small backpack with a few cans of food, drinking water, cold medicine, and a flashlight. It’s like taking out an extra insurance policy for peace of mind, not excessive stockpiling," she said.

picked.t: Missing Vietnamese girl, 13, found dead near German-Polish border
picked.body: Brandenburg police were called to an unoccupied single-family house in Altglietzen, a village of about 400 residents in the town of Bad Freienwalde, around noon on Sunday after a report that someone had broken in, police and prosecutors said in a joint statement, Tagesspiegel reported. The owner had noticed the break-in and alerted police. Inside, officers found the girl's body and a seriously injured man. The statement said the man is believed to have inflicted his injuries himself and is suspected of being responsible for Lisa's death. He used a firearm, according to information obtained by the German Press Agency ( dpa ). The man was in a life-threatening condition in hospital under police guard on the evening of Sunday, and his identity was still unknown, said Michael Petzold, spokesman for the Berlin public prosecutor's office. "It is currently unclear whether he will survive his injuries," Petzold said. He gave no details of the man's injuries or of how the girl died, adding that an autopsy was planned. Homicide units from Berlin's State Criminal Police Office and the Berlin prosecutor's office secured evidence at the scene with Brandenburg police that evening. Investigators were set to return to the house and grounds on Monday to secure further evidence. Lisa is believed to have been dead for some time. A resident said that on the day Lisa disappeared, a car with Berlin license plates stood outside the house for hours with its hazard lights flashing. Other neighbors said they had heard cries for help in recent days, but no one called the police. Lisa left her family's home on Golliner Strasse in Berlin's Marzahn neighborhood on the morning of Nov. 3 to catch a bus from Barnimplatz at around 7:30 a.m. to her school on Sella-Hasse-Strasse, police said. She never arrived. Authorities said they had found no indication that Lisa wanted to leave her family, and a homicide unit took over the case on suspicion of a serious crime. Police went door to door, handed out witness appeals and searched with sniffer dogs and a helicopter. More than 100 officers were deployed on Sunday alone. Until the body was found, there had been no leads suggesting the girl might be 50 km from Berlin, close to the Polish border, Petzold said. The search had focused on Berlin's Marzahn-Hellersdorf borough and the adjacent parts of Brandenburg. Key questions remain open, including how and when Lisa died, who the suspect is and what his motive was. Many of them could go unanswered if he does not survive, since an investigation is closed when the accused dies, according to dpa.

picked.t: Vietnam's top leader calls for stronger AI, quantum technology ties with Japan
picked.body: Speaking at a meeting with Vietnamese scientists, specialists and intellectuals in Japan on Sunday, during his official visit, the leader emphasized their role in connecting expertise, experience and resources to support Vietnam's technological advancement. He stressed that amid profound global changes driven by science - technology, innovation and digital transformation, the Vietnamese intellectual community abroad is playing an increasingly important role, particularly in Japan, one of the world's leading scientific and technological powers. The Vietnam-Japan Comprehensive Strategic Partnership is in a phase of positive, substantive and effective development, underpinned by a high level of political trust across all areas. Science, technology and innovation are emerging as new pillars of bilateral cooperation, he said. The leader briefed the participants on Vietnam’s issuance of various resolutions and decrees to promote the attraction and effective use of overseas Vietnamese experts and intellectuals. A conclusion on attracting and utilizing talent in strategic sectors to support rapid and sustainable development was also adopted at the fourth plenum of the 14th Party Central Committee. He expressed confidence that the Vietnamese expert and intellectual network in Japan will continue to grow and become an important bridge in advancing Vietnam's knowledge- and technology-driven development. The General Secretary and President expressed his desire to hear recommendations from Vietnamese experts and intellectuals in Japan on strengthening the tripartite linkage between the State, businesses and universities to attract more Japanese investment projects with high technological content and added value. He suggested promoting research and development, technology transfer and high-quality human resources training in Vietnam, while strengthening business connections between the two countries. He urged the expansion of networks connecting Vietnamese and Japanese experts to serve as bridges for bilateral cooperation in areas where Japan has strengths and Vietnam has growing needs, such as innovation, space technology, artificial intelligence (AI), semiconductors, quantum technology, marine science and the marine economy, digital technology, rare earth exploration and development, medical technology, advanced biotechnology, and hydrogen-powered high-tech agriculture. Experts were encouraged to share research findings that could help improve labor productivity in Vietnam and offer recommendations on addressing bottlenecks in institutional frameworks, the investment environment, infrastructure, human resources and technological capacity. At the meeting, Vietnamese experts working in semiconductors, AI, quantum technology, robotics and biomedicine shared proposals for developing strategic technologies. They also presented specific products and projects contributing directly to Vietnam's development and promoting bilateral scientific and technological cooperation. Expressing their commitment to the homeland, the experts pledged to contribute to national development in the spirit of Resolution 57 by helping train strong research teams, establish laboratories, promote university-business partnerships and jointly develop technologies and products that Vietnam needs. At the meeting, Vietnamese Ambassador to Japan Pham Quang Hieu said the Vietnamese expert and intellectual community in Japan has grown steadily in both size and quality. There are currently more than 260 Vietnamese scientists in Japan holding professorships, associate professorships or doctoral degrees, while nearly 1,000 experts have been recognized in Japan for their high-level expertise in science, technology and management. Many have gained extensive experience in research, technology development and the commercialization of research findings.

picked.t: 베트남 3대 승차공유社 GSM, 연말맞이 ‘요금 25% 할인’ 프로모션…내년 2월까지
picked.body: (사진=GSM) 베트남 3대  차량호출 플랫폼 중 하나인 그린SM(Green SM, 이하 GSM)이 내년까지 요금 25%를 한시적으로 인하하고, 파트너드라이버에게는 플랫폼 수수로를 면제하는 파격적인 프로모션에 나선다. GSM에 따르면, ‘푸른 겨울, 푸른 미래를 위해(Mua dong xanh-Vi tuong lai xanh)’로 명명된 이번 프로모션은 연말 성수기 이용객들의 교통비 부담을 줄여주기 위해 기획됐다. 이번 프로모션은 자사 자동차·이륜차 호출서비스 이용객에게 요금 25% 자동 할인 혜택 제공을 골자로 한다. 프로모션은 지난 8일 시작됐으며, 내년 2월까지 한시적으로 진행된다. 승객 요금 할인과 더불어 파트너드라이버에게도 파격적인 혜택이 적용된다. 프로모션 기간 파트너드라이버는 플랫폼 수수료(자동차 6%·이륜차 6.7%) 전액이 면제되며, 특히 GSM에서만 활동하는 드라이버들은 승객 요금의 25% 할인 전 전체 요금을 운행 수입으로 보장받을 수 있다. 이 밖에도 GSM은 운행 거리의 2배에 해당하는 만큼 배터리 무료 충전 혜택을 제공하며, GSM 협력사 소속 운전자들은 운행비의 최대 6%까지 지원하는 수입 증대 혜택을 제공받을 수 있다. 이에 대해 팜 녓 민 황(Pham Nhat Minh Hoang) GSM글로벌 총괄대표는 “이번 프로모션은 전기차 호출 서비스 수요 진작과 동시에 파트너드라이버들의 수입을 유지하기 위한 것”이라며 “4개월간 이어지는 프로모션은 연말 이용객들의 교통비 부담을 줄이는 동시에 많은 고객들에게 친환경 차량을 경험할 수 있는 기회가 될 것으로 기대한다”고 밝혔다. GSM은 수익 분배 정책과 플랫폼 수수료 면제, 운행 보너스 프로그램 등을 모두 더할 경우, 파트너드라이버들의 수입이 기존과 비교해 30~50% 늘 것으로 추산했다. GSM에 따르면, 1~9월 운행 횟수는 8억5,000만 회에 육박했는데, 이를 통해 이산화탄소 배출량을 80만 톤 이상 줄인 것으로 추정된다. 이는 3,600만 그루의 나무가 1년 동안 흡수하는 온실가스량과 같은 규모다.
